clue.text: Sitting for a time among children

indicators.note: the pair of pieces is set among the letters of the word for offspring

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in the biblical 'seed of Abraham'

explanation.surface: Someone sits with a group of children for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts A and T inside SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe being in a chair rather than standing, so one is a synonym of the other.

clue.text: Fur is practical when going topless!

indicators.note: losing the top means the word 'is' loses its first letter in this down clue

parts.note: taken as written before its top is removed
practical, in the sense of capable or competent, means able

explanation.surface: A remark that wearing fur is sensible once you take your top off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the I from IS, leaving S, which goes before ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark pelt of a small Asian marten, prized as a luxury fur.

clue.text: As the nuns have lost Elizabeth gives a hand

indicators.note: the nuns 'have lost' a royal abbreviation, so those letters are taken out of their word

parts.note: nuns are called Sisters
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A convent loses a member named Elizabeth, and someone pitches in to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have lost' removes ER from SISTERS, leaving SISTS, which follows AS. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the British monarch's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to help them, which is what lending a hand means.

clue.text: Always on the outside but not unknown

indicators.note: the phrase 'but not' asks for the unknown's letter to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: externally means on the outside
in algebra x is the usual unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A paradox: always on the outside, yet never quite a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' takes X out of EXTERNALLY. X is the algebraic unknown, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean for all time, without end, so the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Customer parking on tar newly spread!

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the freshly spread surface material is in a new arrangement, so its letters with 'on' are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper parks on a car park whose tarmac has just been laid.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'car' but the wordplay needs 'tar', one letter off. 'newly spread' turns ON and TAR into ATRON, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular client of a shop or business, the same as a customer.

clue.text: To be still held by a pole is stranger

indicators.note: the phrase to be still is held, that is enclosed, by the letters for a pole

parts.note: N, north, is one of the magnetic poles
to lie is to stay still and motionless

explanation.surface: Something that keeps still while tied to a post seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts LIE inside A and N. 'stranger' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, someone strange to a place.

clue.text: Regard as a bit more spectacular

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase more spectacular is wanted, a run of letters across its words

explanation.surface: Respect seen as a slight increase in how impressive something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' points to the run moRE SPECTacular.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone highly is to esteem or admire them, so the verbs match.

clue.text: By noon remove unruly sol soldiers — but not ever again

indicators.note: an unruly thing is out of order, so the letters of remove are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: An order to clear out disorderly troops by midday, never to return.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray 'sol' before 'soldiers', a scanning slip that plays no part. 'unruly' shuffles REMOVE into EVERMO, between N and RE (Royal Engineers).
explanation.definitionFit: Nevermore is a poetic word meaning never again, as in Poe's raven.

clue.text: Shamefaced sailor takes a drop!

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to shed is to drop, as a tree drops leaves

explanation.surface: An embarrassed sailor helps himself to a tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a drink for the sailor, but it is the verb, shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed and ashamed, so both words describe a red-faced person.

clue.text: Fail to understand I have shorter message

parts.note: to miss a point is to fail to grasp it
the shortened form of I have is the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone admits failing to grasp a note they received.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I'VE is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter, a formal written communication.

clue.text: Pit duty is not normally simplicity

indicators.note: letters not arranged in their normal order are reshuffled, here pit duty is

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a shift down the coal mine isn't usually straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not normally' rearranges PITDUTYIS. Simplicity here is the sense of foolishness, being simple-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplicity can mean lack of intelligence, being simple, which is foolishness.

clue.text: Note King's new name for palace

indicators.note: letters given a new order are rearranged, here the note and the king's word

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive 's adds no apostrophe, giving the word kings

explanation.surface: A memo: the monarch has given a new name to a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NOTE and KINGS into KENSINGTO, then N follows. Kensington Palace is a London royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Palace is a royal residence in west London.

clue.text: Man removing bails

indicators.note: re-moving the cricket pieces means moving their letters around again

explanation.surface: A cricketer knocks the bails off the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'balls', but the wordplay needs 'bails', the two small crosspieces on top of the stumps in cricket. 'removing' rearranges BAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a man's first name, so the clue's 'man' stands for it.

clue.text: Fan, 50 amps, used by people stripping?

parts.note: to fan air is to blow it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: An electric fan drawing fifty amps, used by some workers in the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people stripping' suggests undressing, but it means stripping old paint, done with a gas torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch is the tool decorators use to burn off old paint, so it serves strippers of paintwork.

clue.text: One warlike president admitted it's fair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the president is admitted, let inside, the word for warlike

parts.note: martial means warlike, as in martial arts

explanation.surface: A warmongering head of state concedes that something is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts P inside MARTIAL, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means unbiased, treating all sides equally, which is what fair means.

clue.text: Old lady in tank travelling from place to place

indicators.note: the elderly woman is placed in the large container

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
a gran, grandmother, is an old lady

explanation.surface: A grandmother rides in a military tank on a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tank' suggests an armoured vehicle, but it is a storage vessel, VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a wanderer with no fixed home, always moving on.

clue.text: Firearm for a man on board?

definitions.meaning: in gangster slang a handgun goes by this name
a chessman standing on the chessboard

explanation.definitionFit: Gangster slang calls a handgun a piece, and chess calls each chessman a piece.

clue.text: See it as possibly the least difficult

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible other arrangement of the letters of see it as

explanation.surface: Someone says you might regard it as the simplest option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SEEITAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest is the superlative of easy, the most simple, least hard.

clue.text: Conservative leader with a record that's foul

indicators.note: the leader of the word Conservative is its first letter

parts.note: a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: A Tory chief with a past record is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to foul up a pipe or drain.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog a drain is to foul it, blocking it up.

clue.text: Objection to locks for piers?

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'
tresses are locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone objects to long hair being cut for a seaside pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piers' suggests seaside jetties, but here it means masonry supports for a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, a pier is a solid support, and a buttress is such a supporting mass of masonry.

clue.text: In competition students And she's fair

indicators.note: the learners are placed in the word for the contest

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in a spelling bee
L is a learner, so two students give two Ls

explanation.surface: A beauty contestant competes among a crowd of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts LL inside BEE. L is the learner plate on British cars, so a learner is a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, so she is fair in the old sense of lovely.

clue.text: Elicit approval during the day before

indicators.note: approval comes during the day before, inside its word

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Getting approval on the day before an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts OK inside EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a response is to call it forth or draw it out.

clue.text: Putting salt in meal I cooked is friendly?

indicators.note: the salt is put in the reshuffled meal and I
cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
an old salt is a sailor, abbreviated AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Seasoning a dish you have cooked yourself is a kindly gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like seasoning, but it is a sailor, AB. 'cooked' turns MEAL I into AMILE, and 'in' puts AB inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured and pleasant, which friendly also describes.

clue.text: Having exchanged one lira on plane, flap!

indicators.note: exchanged letters swap places, so one lira is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone changes their last lira into another currency on board a flight, in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having exchanged' rearranges ONELIRA. 'flap' suggests panic, but it is a flap on an aircraft's wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged surface on an aircraft wing used to control roll.

clue.text: One temporarily in charge of the issue?

definitions.text: One temporarily in charge of the issue?

parts.words: One temporarily in charge of the issue?
parts.note: issue here means offspring, so the person minding children for a while

explanation.surface: Someone holding a matter in their hands for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a topic or problem, but it means children, as in a babysitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A babysitter, shortened, minds the children while parents are out.

clue.text: Happy to be burning hot live outside

indicators.note: the word for live goes outside the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
something burning is lit
H is an abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Glad to be burning hot, alive on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BE round LIT and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree and cheerful, so it is a synonym for glad.
